Wiktor Tomasik — Strange loop in J-space

Current research, 19 October 2026, in The Mind in the Mirror: Self-Models at https://pixedar.github.io/.

A learned reader around a frozen language model forms a 32-number picture and an 8-number control state. A centered-field discrimination game removes the shortcut of identifying a copy by its destination. From organized starts, some runs develop state-dependent movement, mainly through the state changing the reader's query. A shared spotlight gives the reader consequences for the model's predictions, with only weak measured return through the model into the loop.

The best developmental run has normalized state dependence 0.65, compared with 0.002 for a recorded-other-description control. This is a ratio of squared variations, not a probability or fraction of steps. Picture-field correlation +0.81 measures pattern agreement; unscaled vector predictions remain poorly calibrated. Cutting the reader path reduces large movements from 26.6% to 1.2% of steps in that run. Five own-spotlight self-describing runs change 11–16% of top next-token predictions. Loss changes are small and mixed, and the non-self-describing control also changes predictions.

Three later developmental starts reached the regime, following two of five sustained initial small-model runs; these are small, related samples. Copies can converge on shared text. No stable personality or representation of the consequences of attention is established. Native multimodal and behavior follow-ups are exploratory, with explicit controls and limitations. None of these measurements establishes subjective experience.

Earlier distinct branches retain frozen-loop persona drift and invented-past behavior, a rotating time code in a chunked reasoning loop, fed-back forecasts, and a state that selects evidence. The history distinguishes these mechanisms and includes negative causal-map results.

Author: Wiktor Tomasik
